_comment: Friday's capability registry: the TARGET architecture, and what is actually
This file is the contract. Skills, CLAUDE.md and the CLI all read it, so
there is exactly one place that knows whether a capability exists. That
matters because the alternative is what supabase.yml already does with its
hardcoded function list: a description of reality that drifts from reality
and fails silently when it does.
workflow   Riley's front door. Task-shaped, few, appear in `friday help`.
primitive  The engine. Precise, namespaced, for agents and for workflows
to orchestrate. Hidden from `friday help` unless asked for.
STATUS is either `implemented` or `planned`. A planned capability prints
what it will do and exits non-zero. It never pretends to have worked.
THE RULE FOR AGENTS: if you need a planned capability, implementing it in
Friday is the next development task. Do not route around Friday with an ad
hoc shell command — the invariant Friday enforces is the reason it exists.

check.summary: Machine, secrets, project config, repo and fast code checks, ending in one next action.
check.success: Reports every problem it found and names exactly one next action.
check.invariant: Read-only. Must never mutate anything, so it is safe to run when confused.

fix.summary: Format and auto-fix everything that can be fixed without judgement.
fix.blockedBy: The repo has no formatter. Adding one is a separate, deliberate reformat commit.
fix.success: Formatting and auto-fixable lint applied; nothing else touched.
fix.invariant: Only changes that cannot alter behaviour. Never a fix that requires judgement.

test.summary: The full gate: format, lint, types, unit, e2e, export.
test.success: Every gate check passed, or the first failure is reported and the rest are not claimed.
test.invariant: Refuses on first failure. Never reports a partial run as a pass.

preview.riley: Run it locally and look at it.
preview.summary: Start the dev server and open the app.
preview.invariant: Local only. Must never point at a hosted project.

ship.staging.summary: Run the gate, ship to staging, print where to go try it.
ship.staging.mutates: Staging database schema and Edge Functions.
ship.staging.success: Migrations applied, functions deployed, and a receipt recorded tying the staging state to this SHA.
ship.staging.invariant: Runs the gate first and refuses if it fails. The receipt is what makes production promotion verifiable later.

ship.production.summary: Preflight, plain-English diff, snapshot, typed confirmation, then the ordered ship.
ship.production.blockedBy: supabase/refs.json is not filled in, and there is no production gate in the pipeline yet.
ship.production.mutates: PRODUCTION database schema, Edge Functions, and the web client.
ship.production.success: Backend applied and verified, then web deployed, in that order. Reports which halves landed.
ship.production.invariant: Refuses unless staging represents this exact SHA. Snapshots before touching anything. Requires a typed confirmation naming the change. Backend before clients, always — and ordered, not atomic: if the web half fails, production holds new backend and old client, which is safe only because backend changes are backward-compatible by rule.

release.summary: Drive one versioned release across web, iOS and Android.
release.mutates: Version files, tags, and whichever platform lanes are invoked.
release.success: One versioned release exists across the lanes that were asked for.
release.invariant: prepare, submit and release are three distinct verbs and are never collapsed. Publishing needs explicit confirmation naming platform and version.

undo.summary: Print the verified restore command, and how many player attempts it would discard. Never runs it.
undo.mutates: Nothing. It prints and never executes.
undo.success: Prints the verified restore command AND the number of player attempts that restore would discard.
undo.invariant: MUST NOT run the restore. A restore rewinds player data as well as schema, and each player gets one attempt per day, so those players lose their only attempt permanently.

capabilities.summary: What Friday is designed to do, and what is built of it.
capabilities.success: Lists every capability and its status.
capabilities.invariant: Cross-checks the registry against the handler table; reports either kind of drift as a Friday bug.

system.doctor.summary: Is this machine set up? Tools, versions, secrets, and how Friday itself is running.
system.doctor.success: Machine state reported, and Friday's own freshness proven first.
system.doctor.invariant: If the freshness guarantee is broken, say so before anything else — nothing else it reports can be trusted.

system.status.summary: One-screen answer to where everything currently stands.
system.status.success: One screen: branch, backend state per environment, live versions per channel.

quality.format.blockedBy: No formatter in the repo yet.
quality.format.invariant: Blocked until a formatter exists; introducing one is a single deliberate reformat commit, not a side effect.

quality.lint.success: ESLint's real output, not a summary.
quality.lint.invariant: Reports raw output so a caller can act on it.

quality.typecheck.invariant: Distinguish a stale .next build tree from genuine type errors — reporting the first as the second is a false signal.

quality.unit.invariant: Covers the npm workspaces only. supabase/tests does NOT run — see CLAUDE.md.

quality.e2e.invariant: Needs a built app; must say so rather than failing obscurely.

quality.export.summary: Build and validate the static export the native shells package.
quality.export.mutates: Writes and then restores the static export tree.
quality.export.success: Static export builds and validates, and the source tree is restored afterwards.
quality.export.invariant: The native shells package this export. Must assert the source tree was restored — a half-restored tree is worse than a failed build.

quality.gate.summary: Everything above, in order, refusing at the first failure.
quality.gate.success: No regression from the quality baseline, and every check either passed or is named as not run.
quality.gate.invariant: Grandfathered findings are reported, never hidden. Checks that are not implemented are named as NOT COVERED. A gate that quietly covers less than it claims is worse than no gate.

quality.baseline.summary: Show the accepted legacy findings, and whether they have moved. --shrink to reduce; expanding needs an explicit token.
quality.baseline.success: Shows accepted debt and whether it moved.
quality.baseline.invariant: Shrinks freely; grows only with an explicit token. An agent whose new code fails lint must fix the code, not widen the baseline.

docker.up.invariant: Local only, never a hosted project.

docker.down.invariant: Must be safe to call when nothing is running.

docker.status.summary: Is it running, and on which ports.
docker.status.success: Running or not, and on which ports.

docker.doctor.summary: Why the local stack will not start.
docker.doctor.success: Names the specific reason the stack will not start.
docker.doctor.invariant: Read-only. Distinguish Docker-not-running from a port conflict from a bad migration.

backend.status.summary: What is deployed to each hosted project right now.
backend.status.success: What is deployed to each environment right now.
backend.status.invariant: Read-only. Requires supabase/refs.json to be filled in — refuses rather than guessing which project is which.

backend.drift.summary: Where a hosted project disagrees with this repo.
backend.drift.success: Every place a hosted project disagrees with this repo.
backend.drift.invariant: Read-only. This is the command that answers 'is the thing I am looking at actually deployed?' — it must never report clean on incomplete information.

backend.plan.summary: What a deploy would do, in plain English, before it does it.
backend.plan.success: An ordered plan in plain English, including what runs first and what it will affect.
backend.plan.invariant: Read-only. This is what a human reads before confirming a production ship, so it must be understandable by someone who cannot read a migration.

backend.verify.summary: Prove a deploy landed and the invariants still hold.
backend.verify.success: Proves the deploy landed AND the invariants still hold — not merely that the command exited 0.
backend.verify.invariant: 'It deployed' is not success. Verify the resulting state.

backend.activation.summary: Which Edge Functions are live, versus what is on disk.
backend.activation.success: Which Edge Functions are actually live, versus what is on disk.
backend.activation.invariant: This exists because 3 of 27 functions were never deployed for weeks and nothing noticed. Must compare against the functions manifest, not a hardcoded list.

backend.promote.summary: Move a verified staging state to production, through CI.
backend.promote.success: Verified staging state moved to production.
backend.promote.invariant: The primitive under ship.production. Same refusals apply; it is not a way around them.

release.status.summary: What version and build is live on each channel.
release.status.success: Version and build live on each channel, and what is in flight.
release.status.invariant: Read-only. Must distinguish 'in review' from 'live' from 'unknown'.

release.preflight.summary: Verify the repo, gates and credentials are ready to release. Read-only.
release.preflight.success: Repo, gates and credentials are ready. Exits non-zero on any failure.
release.preflight.invariant: Read-only, no public impact. Runs before anything else in a release.

release.prepare.summary: Bump, build and gate. No public impact.
release.prepare.mutates: version.json, native version files, a tag.
release.prepare.success: A version, a SHA and release notes are established once, for all three lanes.
release.prepare.invariant: NO public impact. Establishes the canonical release SHA that every lane must use — no lane may invent its own version.

release.rc.success: An RC exists, tied to the canonical SHA.

release.notes.summary: Assemble release notes from the range.
release.notes.success: Notes assembled from the commit range.

release.tag.invariant: Tags the canonical SHA, never HEAD-at-the-time.

release.web.build.summary: Build the Cloudflare Worker via OpenNext.
release.web.build.success: An OpenNext worker artifact built from the canonical SHA.

release.web.deploy.invariant: PUBLIC IMPACT. Backend must already be deployed and verified — a client must never ship ahead of the schema it needs.

release.web.verify.summary: Prove the live worker is the artifact you built.
release.web.verify.success: The live worker is byte-for-byte the artifact that was built, at the expected SHA.
release.web.verify.invariant: Deploy succeeding is not the same as the right thing being live.

release.web.rollback.summary: Redeploy the previous worker. The only channel where rollback is possible — mobile is forward-only.
release.web.rollback.success: The previous worker is live again.
release.web.rollback.invariant: PUBLIC IMPACT. Web is the ONLY channel that can be rolled back; mobile is forward-only. Never imply otherwise.

release.ios.build.summary: Export, cap sync, archive, signed IPA.
release.ios.build.success: A signed IPA built from the canonical SHA.
release.ios.build.invariant: Local because it needs Xcode and signing material CI does not have. No public impact. Never invents a version.

release.ios.upload.summary: Upload the IPA to App Store Connect.
release.ios.upload.success: The build appears in ASC processing.
release.ios.upload.invariant: No PUBLIC impact. Upload succeeding is not submission.

release.ios.submit.success: ASC reports the build as waiting for review.
release.ios.submit.invariant: No public impact yet — review is not release. Submits the exact build from the canonical SHA. Successful upload is NOT successful review; Friday verifies the resulting ASC state rather than assuming.

release.ios.status.summary: Where the build is in TestFlight and review.
release.ios.status.success: Where the build sits in TestFlight and review.
release.ios.status.invariant: Read-only. Distinguish processing, waiting for review, in review, approved, and live.

release.android.build.success: A signed AAB built from the canonical SHA.
release.android.build.invariant: Local because it needs Gradle and the keystore. No public impact. Never invents a version.

release.android.upload.summary: Upload the AAB to a Play track.
release.android.upload.success: The AAB is on the track.

release.android.rollout.summary: Advance a staged rollout percentage. Public impact.
release.android.rollout.success: The rollout is at the requested percentage.
release.android.rollout.invariant: PUBLIC IMPACT, and it is one-way — a staged rollout can be halted but not un-shipped. Requires explicit confirmation naming the percentage.

secrets.list.summary: Every secret Friday knows about, and where each one resolves from. Never prints a value.
secrets.list.success: Every secret Friday knows about and where each resolves from.
secrets.list.invariant: Presence and source only. NEVER decrypts, never prints a value, never triggers a Keychain prompt.

secrets.set.summary: Store a secret in the Keychain.
secrets.set.invariant: Never echoes the value. Never writes a secret to the repo or to a shell history.

docs.generate.summary: Regenerate the parts of the skills that describe Friday's command surface.
docs.generate.success: Generated sections regenerated from the registry.
docs.generate.invariant: Only rewrites clearly delimited generated blocks. Never touches hand-written prose.

docs.check.summary: Fail if the skills disagree with this registry.
docs.check.success: Every command a skill names resolves to a declared capability.
docs.check.invariant: Checks only what CAN be checked. Does not claim to verify that prose is correct or complete.
